title: Stopping
hook: rest is a commandment, not a reward
tomorrow: don Ernesto is hanging up his apron. so what's he for now?

segments.voice: Yesterday, honest business: one stone in the bag, a yes that means yes, and Zacchaeus paying back fourfold. The line was honest dealing.

The laptop is still open at eleven. One more email, one more chapter, one more shift. Work has a way of never quite ending, so rest waits for the day it does, which doesn't come. Even a day off gets spent catching up. Somewhere along the way, rest turned into a prize: you get it once you've earned it. The Ten Commandments see it differently. In them, rest isn't a reward at all. It's an order.
screen: `STILL OPEN AT ELEVEN.` → `REST AS A PRIZE?` → `REST AS AN ORDER.`

segments.voice: In the commandments, rest doesn't come after the work is done. It comes by the calendar. Exodus, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God." Six days of work, then a stop, finished or not. And look who gets the stop: son and daughter, the servants, the animals, the stranger staying with you. Nobody earns it. Even the donkey gets the day. Rest isn't the prize at the end of the list; it's built into the week whether the list is done or not. Deuteronomy gives the reason: remember that you were a slave in Egypt. Slaves don't get a day off; free people do. Rest is how a freed people keeps remembering it's free. Jesus, in an argument about the sabbath, puts it plainly: "The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath." A gift, not a trap. And when his friends are so busy they have no time even to eat, he tells them, "Come apart into a desert place, and rest a little." The Catechism calls the day of rest a protest against slavery to work and the worship of money. Catholics keep it on Sunday, setting aside work that crowds out worship, family and real rest. That's the commandment in miniature: the work isn't done, and you stop anyway.
screen: `REST BY THE CALENDAR.` · `EVEN THE DONKEY GETS THE DAY.` · `MADE FOR MAN.` · `COME APART AND REST A LITTLE.` · then, large: `STOP ON TIME.`

segments.voice: Choose the hour your work stops today, school, job or screen, and say it out loud once, plainly, the way you'd say a promise to a friend. Then let the unfinished things sit where they are. If one keeps tugging at you, write it down for tomorrow and leave it there. If you pray, you can hand that pile to God for the night.
Stopping. Ending work on purpose and on time, because in the commandments rest is given to everyone, not earned by finishing.
Pocket this: stop on time, because the commandment gave the day to the donkey and the stranger too. Rest well.
